headline: High: shared-bus Pipecat plus writable Marketingskills creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk by default; no direct evidence of stronger isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can write files and uses shared skill/context files; agent B explicitly uses a shared bus and shared state across instances. That creates a plausible default pathway for A-originated content to reach B as trusted input. No direct evidence of a parser exploit, so I choose medium rather than low because the bridge is broader than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instructions or markup into a shared file or bus consumed by agent_b, then agent_b may treat them as trusted input.
IF agent_b reads shared-state content without provenance checks, then injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Separate agent_a and agent_b into distinct workspaces.
Disable shared-bus ingestion for untrusted content.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.
Require a human review step before agent_b executes file-derived instructions.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on the shared bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing and product-marketing context and can read/write files; agent B processes text, conversation state, analytics, and can call multiple third-party APIs by default. A shared workspace or bus could move sensitive marketing context into B’s outbound requests. The exact leak path is not fully documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium, not low.
conditions: IF agent_a stores confidential marketing context in a shared file or message, then agent_b can ingest it.
IF agent_b forwards conversation state to an external API, then shared content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive marketing files out of any shared directory.
Use a redaction step before agent_b API calls.
Restrict agent_b to local-only providers for sensitive runs.
Rotate or segregate credentials used by each agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A supports multiple instances and can write the filesystem; agent B also supports multiple instances with shared bus/shared state. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and state races are plausible by default, and the rubric treats overlapping unrestricted writes as high risk. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared state, then last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
IF either agent modifies git or other mutable state without locks, then concurrent edits can clobber each other.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo or workspace.
Snapshot the workspace before parallel execution.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces marketing content/context, and agent B handles text/conversation state and can route outputs through LLM and transport services. That makes it plausible that B will treat A’s output as authoritative unless explicitly verified. The pair lacks documented verification controls, so the interaction exists in default workflows but is not proven to trigger harmful downstream actions.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as prompt context or source text without verification, then errors can cascade.
IF agent_b triggers downstream actions from A-generated claims, then incorrect marketing facts can be propagated.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before agent_b consumes agent_a output.
Mark A-generated content as untrusted by default.
Limit agent_b to summarization rather than action-taking.
Require citations for any factual claims passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is a marketing skill with file-based context and allowlisted egress; agent B is a voice/chat framework with broad third-party service integrations. The profiles do not show a specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so only a generic compliance-gap risk is visible. I do not cite only one agent because the concern is the pairwise flow between A’s content and B’s external services.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into agent_a content and then sent through agent_b external services, then policy mismatch may occur.
IF retention settings differ between the two agents' downstream services, then deletion/export obligations may be inconsistent.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document which downstream services agent_b may call.
Set explicit retention limits on all external services.
Review data-processing terms before enabling external APIs.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
